prompt: In triangular frame $ABC$, a brace $\overline{DE}$ runs parallel to the base $\overline{BC}$, with $D$ on $\overline{AB}$ and $E$ on $\overline{AC}$. If $AD = 4$, $DB = 6$, and $AE = 6$, find $EC$.
hint: A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides proportionally.

hints.text: A line parallel to one side of a triangle cuts the other two sides proportionally.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try friendly numbers: if $AD = 2$, $DB = 4$ and $AE = 3$, then $\frac{2}{4} = \frac{3}{EC}$ cross-multiplies to $EC = 6$. Build your proportion the same way, top piece over bottom piece on each side.

explanation: Because $\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}$, the corresponding angles make $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$, and the brace splits the two sides proportionally.
Check the whole sides too: $\frac{AD}{AB} = \frac{4}{10}$ and $\frac{AE}{AC} = \frac{6}{15}$, and both equal $0.4$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Work with the whole triangles
steps: Cross-multiply: $4 \cdot AC = 60$, so $AC = 15$. Then $EC = AC - AE = 15 - 6 = 9$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap answer is 15 — writing $\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{AE}{AC}$ mixes a PART-to-PART ratio on the left with a PART-to-WHOLE ratio on the right, and lands you on $AC$ instead of $EC$.
Keep both sides of a proportion the same kind: piece-to-piece with piece-to-piece ($\frac{4}{6} = \frac{6}{EC}$), or piece-to-whole with piece-to-whole. Match the types and $EC = 9$ falls out.
